summary: Quarterly renewal and expansion check-in. Customer interested in upgrading to additional dedicated capacity, adding two EU regions (London, Frankfurt), and extending contract by 12 months with a committed capacity discount. Discussion covered latency targets, failover between regions, SSO/KMS compliance, and benchmark plan for validating throughput. Redwood to send pricing and schedule benchmarks; customer to confirm regions and internal signoffs.
topics: Dedicated capacity sizing and burst options
transcript:
[00:00] Jenna (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Jenna from Redwood; Marcus our SE; Ava from CSM. Tom?
[00:08] Tom (Peregrine): Hey Jenna, hey Marcus, Sara and Alex are here too. Thanks for squeezing us in.
[00:14] Jenna: Great. The goal for today is a renewal + expansion check-in — figure out committed capacity, regions, and next steps for the contract extension. Roughly 30-40 minutes ok?
[00:22] Sara (CTO): Yep, sounds good. We're roughly three months out from renewal and want to lock in pricing and regions soon, internal procurement needs lead time.
[00:30] Marcus (Redwood SE): Cool. Quick sanity check — current footprint is dedicated pool on us-east-1, right? Running models for routing, chat ops, and an embedding pipeline?
[00:38] Alex (Infra): Correct. We keep the bulk inference in us-east-1 with a smaller fallback in us-west. Peak is about 600 qps for short conversations, but embeddings spike during nightly batches.
[00:48] Jenna: Ok. For renewal options we usually present a 12-month committed capacity with a tiered discount; add-ons for burst capacity and cross-region replication. Any target latency SLOs you're aiming for?
[00:58] Tom: Latency pre-90th at 120ms for our lightweight chat routes; heavy long-context prompts can be higher but we'd like to be under 400ms if possible. Cost is also a hard constraint — procurement wants to see unit economics.
[01:08] Marcus: Good to know. Our dedicated instances can be tuned for that. If you want EU regions we can provision g4/g5 equivalents in London and Frankfurt, and configure smart routing so low-latency requests go to closest region with fallback to us-east if capacity constrained.
[01:20] Priya (Security): From a security perspective we need SOC2 evidence, KMS integration for keys, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. We also need SSO via SAML and RBAC controls.
[01:32] Ava (CSM): We generally include those in Private/Dedicated packages — SSO, RBAC, and audit log integrations are supported; Marcus can add specifics.
[01:38] Marcus: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS and can push audit logs to AWS CloudWatch or a forwarder. There's a small onboarding window for key rotations but it's standard.
[01:46] Sara: One thing — compliance sometimes blocks cross-border data flows. If we spin up London/Frankfurt, we need to be sure embeddings and logs don't leave EU for EU-captured traffic.
[01:56] Jenna: That's a common ask. We can configure region-level routing and data residency so requests originating from EU stay in EU regions; model KV cache and prefix caching can be isolated to region. We'll note that in the contract.
[02:08] Tom: Great. On capacity sizing — we've been eyeing a 2x increase in committed capacity given expected product launches. What's the delta in unit price if we double capacity?
[02:18] Jenna: I'll send a pricing sheet but ballpark, committed 2x typically drops per-token unit cost by 18-25% depending on model mix. There's also an option to add burst pool that charges only when used.
[02:28] Alex: For burst capacity, how seamless is failover? We can't have manual steps when latency spikes.
[02:34] Marcus: We offer automatic burst routing; requests are routed based on policy. There's a small cold-start for some model variants, but we can pre-warm instances for critical routes. Also smart batching helps under load.
[02:46] Tom: Can we run a benchmark in staging that mimics our peak—embedding batches + 600 qps chat—to validate both latency and cost?
[02:52] Marcus: Absolutely. We'll coordinate with Alex on traffic patterns. Suggest we run an end-to-end test including EU regions once provisioned.
[02:58] Sara: Timeline: procurement wants signed terms in 6 weeks. That means we need the pricing and contract by next week to allow review and legal back-and-forth.
[03:08] Jenna: Understood. We'll prioritize. I'll send a draft renewal with expansion SKUs by 2026-02-02.
[03:12] Priya: Also please include details on encryption at rest, KMS key ownership, and the retention window for logs — we have a 7-year requirement for audit trails in certain workflows.
[03:20] Marcus: We'll include the retention options. Audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM and Redwood retains minimal traces per policy. We'll provide SOC2 certs and whitepapers.
[03:28] Tom: Another question — we're evaluating Anthropic and Google Cloud AI for some latency-sensitive routes. How does Redwood compare on real-world latency and cost?
[03:36] Jenna: Generally Redwood's dedicated offering focuses on predictable latency and cost. Public APIs can be cheaper for bursty workloads but less predictable. Marcus can run comparative benchmarks against public endpoints if useful.
[03:46] Marcus: We can do that; though note model variants and quantization options will affect latency. For your workload, dedicated instances with optimized kernels should outperform standard public endpoints at 95th percentile.
[03:56] Alex: Any limitations on model weights or custom models in dedicated? We plan to run a fine-tuned variant for routing.
[04:02] Marcus: We support hosting custom weights as long as licensing allows. There are some constraints on size for certain instance types; we can recommend quantization profiles or sharded configurations.
[04:12] Sara: Ok. For EU data residency, what's the onboarding lead time to get London and Frankfurt brought up?
[04:18] Jenna: Typical provisioning for dedicated regions is 3-4 weeks, assuming we have a signed order and region capacity. If you're okay with conservative estimates, budgeting 4 weeks is safe.
[04:26] Tom: Procurement needs to see the dates. If we sign by early February, regions could be live by March. That timeline works.
[04:32] Jenna: Great. On contract length — you mentioned 12 months extension?
[04:36] Tom: Yes, we prefer 12 months with the option to renew at the end. We might negotiate a 24-month for deeper discounts but let's start with 12.
[04:44] Jenna: Makes sense. We'll propose a 12-month committed term with an optional conversion to 24 if you commit to an extended discount.
[04:50] Priya: On compliance docs, please also share penetration testing reports and any certifications for the infra providers used.
[04:56] Marcus: We'll include third-party pen test summaries and a list of underlying infra providers and their assurances.
[05:02] Tom: Ok so next steps recap? Jenna to send pricing and contract draft; Marcus to run benchmark plan with Alex; Tom to confirm regions and compliance constraints; Priya will share specific retention/legal constraints with Jenna's team.
[05:12] Jenna: Exactly. I'll also attach our SOC2 and KMS integration doc. Are there any other blockers?
[05:18] Sara: Not from engineering beyond the benchmark and region confirmation.
[05:22] Alex: We'll coordinate with Marcus on test credentials and traffic patterns.
[05:26] Jenna: Awesome. Let's aim to reconvene after benchmarks — suggest a 30-minute follow-up the week of 2026-02-16.
[05:34] Tom: Works for us. Thanks everyone.
[05:36] Jenna: Thanks all — I'll follow up via email with the pricing and contract. Bye.
[05:40] [call ended]
